additional_concerns: Exposure definitions and channel examples are delegated to the supplied aggregate-exposure fact; the formula does not implement asset identification, look-through, valuation or aggregation. These omissions limit implementation coverage but do not by themselves contradict the classification rule.

The source makes indirect-exposure examples non-exhaustive and subject to SFC updates. An upstream assessment that treats BDCs, CLOs and derivatives as an exhaustive list would introduce an unsupported restriction.

Footnote 1 identifies a separate 15% direct-investment limit under UT Code 7.3. The classification formula neither checks that limit nor establishes investment-limit compliance. The limit must not be used to cap actual exposure when applying the classification threshold.

The conflict-anywhere runtime rule is an additional evidentiary policy, not a requirement stated in the circular. It can block classification despite an independently established threshold or designation route; distinguish that evaluation block from a legal classification outcome.

The source does not specify designation commencement, expiry or revocation rules. The assessment-time convention requires evidence of an operative designation without inventing additional validity requirements.
The three supplied missing dependency IDs have no authority-title mapping. None can reliably be assigned to a particular external authority.
